svg.text: commit(msg, author) — six steps, no staging area
writes straight into workingDirectory — there is no index to stage into
whole-file compare → ADD / MODIFY / DELETE per path
every file → sha1(content) → Blob (existing hash ⇒ silently deduped)
then sha1 over the sorted path\0blobHash canonical form → Tree
exactly ONE parent — the current HEAD. Immutable once built.
id comes from a counter, not from hashing the commit's own content
the branch pointer moves. Nothing else in the repo changed.
Note step 6 is the ONLY mutation. Steps 1-5 are append-only: new blobs, a new
tree, a new commit. History is never rewritten — moving a pointer is the commit. ✓
THE COMMIT DAG — branches are pointers, arrows point BACKWARD
Every arrow points from a CHILD to its PARENT.
A commit knows where it came from; it never knows its children.
That is why the graph is append-only and immutable. ✓
so from m001 you see c005,
merge(branch) — four outcomes, decided in this order
0. guards: not self · branch exists · working dir CLEAN
a dirty tree throws before anything is touched — no half-merge
1. ours == theirs, or theirs is an ancestor of ours
→ throw "already up to date" — nothing to bring in
2. OURS is an ancestor of theirs → FAST-FORWARD
return theirHead unchanged; no new commit is created at all
the branch pointer just slides forward — this is the cheap case
findMergeBase(ours, theirs) → base · union all paths → decide each
conflict-free ⇒ new Commit(mNNN, parents=[ours, theirs], mergedTree)

CONFLICT
both diverged from base

svg.text: null is a legal value: it means "the file does not exist here", so
adds and deletes fall out of the SAME four rules — no special cases. ✓
Any conflict aborts the WHOLE merge with an exception listing the
paths. No markers, no MERGING state, no per-file resolution.

g.text: WHY THREE WAYS AND NOT TWO?
Compare only ours vs theirs and you cannot tell an EDIT from a
non-edit. If they differ, who wins? You would have to ask a human
about every single differing file.
The BASE turns "different" into "who changed it". If one side still
matches the base, that side did nothing — so the other side wins,
automatically. Conflicts shrink to genuinely contested files only.
FINDING THE BASE — and where it is imprecise
collectAncestors(A) into a HashSet, then BFS out from B and
return the first id that is in the set. O(V+E) both ways.
BFS from B means "fewest hops from B", which is the right
answer for the simple two-branch case drawn above.
It is NOT a true LCA on criss-cross histories, where Git falls
back to a recursive merge of multiple bases. Name the gap.
THE FOUR FOLLOW-UPS THIS DIAGRAM INVITES
• "Add a staging area" → a second Map between workingDirectory and commit(); commit()
then snapshots the INDEX, and status() reports staged vs unstaged separately.
• "Line-level diff" → swap Diff.between for an LCS; the merge rules do not change.
• "Resolvable conflicts" → return a MergeResult (merged + conflicts) instead of throwing.
• "Hash the commit too" → sha1(tree + parents + author + message) and the id becomes
tamper-evident — that is what makes a real Git history verifiable.
